title: WMI-Spawned PowerShell Execution with Privilege Escalation Context
description: WmiPrvSE.exe (PID 2876) running as NT Authority/Network Service (S-1-5-20) spawned powershell.exe (PID 8712) running as 'spsql' (Domain Admins). WMI was invoked remotely with explicit 'spsql' credentials, consistent with lateral WMI execution (T1047). Child process PS (8712) command line was wiped (args='-') — deliberate anti-forensics to hide the WMI payload.

change_from_pre: Enhanced with WmiPrvSE SID context and cmdline wipe anti-forensics note

title: Two-Stage PowerShell Chain via SysWOW64
description: powershell.exe (PID 8712, 64-bit) spawned powershell.exe (PID 5848) from c:\windows\syswow64\windowspowershell\v1.0\ with '-Version 5.1 -s -NoLogo -NoProfile'. The '-s' flag puts PowerShell into server mode (PowerShell remoting). Using SysWOW64 switches to a 32-bit process, consistent with bypassing 64-bit AMSI or loading 32-bit shellcode.

title: Staged Payload Execution: p.exe in \Windows\Temp\Perfmon\
description: cmd.exe (PID 5948) executed c:\windows\temp\perfmon\p.exe. Payload staged in a temp subdirectory named 'Perfmon' to blend with legitimate performance monitoring activity. filescan shows the file object \Windows\Temp\Perfmon\p.exe and four separate directory handles to \Windows\Temp\Perfmon, indicating persistent staging. Prefetch files confirm multiple rundll32.exe executions (four distinct hashes) consistent with shellcode loading.

title: rundll32.exe Abuse for Shellcode Execution (Multiple Instances)
description: Nine rundll32.exe processes spawned across the attack chain — six from powershell.exe (PID 5848) and three from p.exe (PID 8260) — all with blank command lines. Blank cmdlines combined with parent=attacker_process is the hallmark of in-memory shellcode injection via CreateRemoteThread or NtCreateThread. Four distinct rundll32 prefetch hashes in filescan confirm executions from different module paths.

title: Code Injection in p.exe: 1.9MB Private RWX VAD (No File Backing)
description: malfind reports a PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE VadS region in p.exe (PID 8260) at 0x2be0000-0x2dc0fff spanning 481 committed pages (~1.9MB) with PrivateMemory=1 and no file backing. This is a textbook reflective shellcode or staged payload region. The hexdump is all underscores (paged out of the physical capture) but the region attributes alone are conclusive.

title: OUTLOOK.EXE Malfind Hits — FALSE POSITIVE (RETRACTED)
description: RETRACTED. Two PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE regions in OUTLOOK.EXE (PID 8128) initially appeared suspicious. Both regions begin with byte sequence 64 74 72 52 00 00 00 00 (ASCII: 'dtrR'), which is a known Outlook Distributed Transaction Record memory allocation signature, not injected shellcode. No PE header (no MZ/4D5A). Classification: benign false positive.
tool_output: malfind.txt: PID 8128 both regions hexdump begin 64 74 72 52 (dtrR). Self-correction skill FP table confirms this pattern.
change_from_pre: RETRACTED — was UNCONFIRMED; confirmed as known FP pattern
